agent: Task 27 — Stretch Goal B: Template / Site Registry Foundation
objective: A filesystem-only registry that INDEXES the templates and customer sites already on disk — register, list, read back, rebuild — without becoming a second source of truth, without a database and without a UI.

placement.why: The registry spans TWO subsystem namespaces — recon-templates (src/recon-template) and release-projects (src/release) — so it belongs to neither. src/editor/registry.ts was the audit's suggestion, but no src/editor exists and no UI is built here; creating that directory would name a component that does not exist. src/registry/ is a peer module directory, which is this repo's one and only structural idiom (src/release/, src/regions/, src/seo/, src/theme/ …).

storage.dataRootOverride: every entry point takes an optional { dataRoot } (src/registry/scan.ts:34-41); the default is "data". The suite uses it to work in data/.smoke-registry-<pid>.
storage.whyDotPrefixed: `.registry` can never be mistaken for a host folder by the scanner, which is the same convention the smoke suites' data/.smoke-<name>-<pid> scratch dirs already rely on (src/registry/scan.ts:47-58 skips every dot-prefixed entry).
storage.machineLocal: data/ is gitignored, so the index is machine-local by construction — which is exactly why it must be rebuildable, and is.

The entry records routePolicyApplied=false and reports slotizedRouteCount = routeCount, structureOnlyRouteCount = 0 — TRUE BY DEFINITION for a compile with no policy (default scope core-reconstruct), not a measurement, and labelled as such at src/registry/types.ts:63-71 and src/registry/scan.ts:122-126.

siteRegistryFields.keyIsNotSiteId: siteId is NOT unique on disk today. Every pre-Task-27 project has its siteId adapted from the host at load time (src/release/instance.ts:128-160), so the two legacy linear.app projects both adapt to siteId `linear.app`. The key is therefore the directory identity (siteKey); the collision is REPORTED as a registry warning (src/registry/scan.ts:234) and readSite() on an ambiguous siteId returns null rather than an arbitrary project (src/registry/store.ts:293-299).
siteRegistryFields.nameIsDerived: `name` is derived from siteId, not stored. A registry-only display name would be a fact the registry could not rebuild from disk — i.e. exactly the second source of truth this goal forbids. See changeRequests[0] for the field that would fix it properly.

secondSourceOfTruthAvoided: Every field is copied or counted from an artifact another subsystem owns, `read*` re-derives from that artifact and returns the derived entry (reporting `indexAgreed:false` when the cached one disagreed), an artifact that was never registered still reads via a scan, and `rebuildRegistry` recreates both index files from a scan alone — so the index is a cache whose loss costs only scan time.

apiSurface.derive: templateEntryFromDisk (scan.ts:92), siteEntryFromDisk (scan.ts:191), scanTemplates, scanSites, listHosts, siteRegistryWarnings
apiSurface.index: loadTemplateRegistry/loadSiteRegistry (a missing file is the EMPTY registry, never an error), saveTemplateRegistry/saveSiteRegistry
apiSurface.register: registerTemplate (store.ts:155), registerSite (store.ts:172) — upsert by key, entries kept lexically sorted
apiSurface.list: listTemplates, listSites — read the cache, which is the only reason the cache exists
apiSurface.read: readTemplate (store.ts:215), readSite (store.ts:263) → ResolvedEntry<T> { entry, resolvedFrom: artifact|index, registered, indexAgreed, artifactMissing }
apiSurface.helpers: sitesWithSiteId (every project sharing one siteId), entriesAgree (key-sorted JSON comparison)

conflictResolution.implementation: readTemplate/readSite use the cached entry ONLY to learn which directory to look in, then re-derive from that directory and return the fresh entry with indexAgreed = entriesAgree(cached, fresh). If the cached directory is gone, a scan is tried before giving up. Only when both fail is the stale entry returned, and then resolvedFrom is "index" and artifactMissing is true, so a dangling pointer can never be mistaken for a live artifact.
conflictResolution.listingIsExplicitlyStale: listTemplates/listSites return the cache verbatim and do NOT re-derive — that is what makes listing cheap. Check 27B.19 pins this so the difference is deliberate and visible, not an accident.

changeRequests.change: add an optional `displayName: z.string().min(1).optional()` to ReleaseProjectSchema, set by `release:prepare --name`
changeRequests.why: The site registry needs a human-facing name. Today it DERIVES `name` from siteId, because a name stored only in the index would be a fact that could not be rebuilt from disk — the exact second-source-of-truth this goal forbids. Once the field exists, src/registry/scan.ts:200 changes to `project.displayName ?? project.siteId` and nameSource gains an `authored` value. Purely additive; every existing project keeps loading.

changeRequests.change: after the project is written, call `registerSite(projectDir)` from src/registry/index.js
changeRequests.why: Registration is currently a library call nothing invokes automatically, so the index only exists once someone builds it. Wiring prepare (and src/cli-compile-recon-template.ts for registerTemplate) makes the index self-maintaining. Deliberately NOT done here: both files belong to other agents, and the registry is correct without it because `read*` falls back to a scan and `rebuildRegistry` recovers everything.

changeRequests.change: after the compile writes its run directory, call `registerTemplate(runDir)` from src/registry/index.js
changeRequests.why: Same reason as above, for the template half.

limitations: NO CLI. The registry is a library plus a suite; there is no `pnpm registry:list`. Adding one is a new src/cli-registry.ts and one package.json line, but the brief said keep it small and a CLI was not asked for.

NO automatic registration. Nothing in the pipeline calls registerTemplate/registerSite yet — see changeRequests 2 and 3. Until then the honest workflow is `rebuildRegistry()`, which is O(number of run directories) and reads two small JSON files per template.

NO preview thumbnails. The audit noted `preview` as the one genuinely missing template field, derivable from the 1,384 existing PNGs. Not built: it needs a screenshot-selection policy, which is a design decision, not an indexing one.

NO locking and NO atomic writes — consistent with the rest of the repo, which has neither. Two processes registering at once can lose one entry (last writer wins on the whole file). The consequence is bounded by design: a lost entry is recovered by a rebuild.
`name` is siteId until src/release/types.ts gains a displayName (changeRequest 1).
The index is machine-local because data/ is gitignored. It is not shared, not committed, and not a deployment artifact.

A template directory that fails to parse is SKIPPED with a warning on the scan result rather than aborting it (src/registry/scan.ts:150-153, and scan.ts:224-227 for sites). A caller that ignores `warnings` will silently see a short list; no current caller does.
readSite/readTemplate scan the whole data root on a cache miss. That is cheap at today's 6 templates / 5 projects and would need an index-first strategy at thousands.
followUps: Wire registerTemplate/registerSite into the compile and prepare CLIs (changeRequests 2, 3) so the index maintains itself.
Add `pnpm registry:list` (templates and sites, one line each) once an operator actually needs to read it outside a test.
Add `displayName` to ReleaseProject (changeRequest 1) and stop deriving `name`.

Give the legacy linear.app projects distinct siteIds, or accept the collision permanently — the registry now names it out loud (27B.7) instead of letting two customer sites share an identity silently, which is the failure the pre-overnight audit reported at line 346.
Template preview images, once a screenshot-selection policy exists.
